## Body

BLOCK at c0cae51578ca534b23e7fa3e0ca43fe1b7d5dff9, round 1.

B322-01 — new ACKs can write the legacy match-any-sender key.
The specialized enqueue, carrying enqueue and note_delivered paths reject a
missing sender. Generic Queue::enqueue does not, and ack_delivery reads the
derived dedupe_sender and passes it to record_delivered without require_sender
(`crates/store/src/queue.rs:579-623,1837-1887,1949-1982`).
An isolated real-SQLite witness enqueues a delivery job with payload {}, claims
and ACKs it. ACK succeeds, writing one NEW sender_seat='' row. A named sender's
own same-ID message then returns AlreadyDelivered(ReaderRead), losing its body.
Thus the migration's wildcard is not confined to legacy rows. The fake ACK has
the same guard gap (`crates/testkit/src/fakes.rs:1554-1581`).
Scope: this is a public store-invariant hole; no live caller-facing exploit was
demonstrated. It falsifies the stated new-row invariant. Refuse this path before
it can create a wildcard; retain the actual legacy-row compatibility brake.

B322-02 — terminal control refusal replay still ignores the sender.
arrive_control finds delivery.outcome by recipient and msg_id, and immediately
returns a recorded control refusal without comparing sender identity
(`crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:1048-1080`). The new live-job key therefore
does not protect this negative replay path.
Witness: the target's own control is refused; its exact same-sender retry
correctly repeats that refusal. The target's parent then sends its own control
under the same id. It receives the first refusal and no new control is queued.
Self and recorded parent are both valid actors for this command
(`crates/core/src/control.rs:87-98`). The assembled-service probe does not bypass
identity to assert that unrelated callers can control the seat; the issue is
that two legitimately distinct actors share an outcome cache. Carry sender
identity through the refusal evidence and lookup while preserving same-sender
refusal replay.

Migration answers:
- PASS: the ledger rebuild keeps every existing row's seq and original content;
  jobs are altered/indexed, not discarded. The embedded sqlx migration runs
  transactionally. An injected SQL error after the new ledger copy and before
  old-table removal rolled back the table rename/rebuild, generated column,
  indexes and version. Old rows/schema and v49 remained; no migration50 success
  was recorded. Two later real boot-path opens migrated once, retained the rows,
  and returned quick_check=ok.
- Idempotence belongs to the migration ledger / open path. The SQL file is not
  intended to be manually executed twice; the second open does not rerun it.
- A v49 binary refuses a v50 DB before running migrations, and its public store
  operations refuse version skew. Verified the v49 source's found>SCHEMA_VERSION
  branch and the current guard, plus the existing future-schema refusal test.
  No downgrade compatibility is promised or attempted.
- The '' legacy match is a BRAKE: removing it can only permit more delivery.
  A new '' delivered row is precisely the invariant violation B322-01, not an
  intended second class of wildcard data.

Identity / held-path answers:
- Body live-row, delivery-ledger, direct transport compensation, native recovery,
  held count and expiry queries now include sender. Body retries from the same
  sender collapse; two senders' same id is two messages. Recipient and originating
  machine stay independently scoped. Non-delivery job kinds keep the old identity.
- Role replies use their own id; role requeue preserves the requester; boot and
  reached/limit probes match requester or pij-bg. The role-recovery wrong-sender
  test passed. Daemon notice admitted checks now use pij-bg; the body-message
  park-notice squat regression passed.
- Decision preparation pins the answering actor, and supersede mints a new
  answer id only after deliberately unscoped terminal/in-transit vetoes. The
  inspected path does not silently let a replacement parent retry the same
  prepared intent under a new sender. FYI identity intentionally remains
  (origin,id); this PR does not promise sender-scoped FYI identity.
- F260 native-held cases passed: restart/renewal delivers once; expired bodies
  never recover; a same-sender copy still in flight defers expiry; another
  sender's same-id copy does not suppress the first sender's expiry; and
  same-id messages for two recipients each recover once.
- Settled-expiry suppression is keyed by park sequence, not merely job id, so
  a later park of the same job is a different record. It eliminates the repeated
  native-lock/queue-write path, not the history enumeration or all read cost.

Cost / integration:
No new periodic tick, subscriber or process launch. The existing park sweep is
every sixty seconds over its twenty-four-hour lookback. A settled hit saves the
native lock and queue transaction, but its latest_matching_message lookup can
still visit sender/kind history and notify performs upstream reads. Three expiry
EXISTS subprobes are indexed; the ledger IN(sender,'') can use two point keys.
VIRTUAL sender keys still incur JSON parsing and index maintenance.
Performance's exact-head optimized store-open receipt measured 0.796449 s and
0.576329 s on two clean copies, preserving 46,061 jobs and 77,452 ledger rows with
original-column hashes and quick_check=ok. This is the release store-open part
of bounce cost, not a live-daemon bounce or an upper bound. I did not duplicate
that timing or access the production database.
The two PR commits apply cleanly atop the stated main baseline; no unresolved
merge hunk. Diff whitespace check and exact-head freeze passed.
